This figure includes all non-voided orders across the shop's history. Please note that this total does not account for any product returns, discounts, or operating expenses.

results.question: How many orders were placed online versus in store?

results.question: Which product has the highest price?

results.answer: The Trench Coat has the highest price in your shop at $269.95 AUD. This price is based on the current list price (including GST) of its variant.
results.assumptions: Interpreting 'price' as the current list price (`variants.price`, GST-inclusive) of any variant belonging to the product.

results.question: How many refunds have been issued?

results.question: How many units have we sold in total?

results.question: What are our top 5 products by units sold?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, SUM(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top-selling product by units is the One-Piece Swimsuit with 4043 units sold, followed by the Straw Hat (3619), Leather Belt (2667), Linen Wrap Skirt (1804), and Shirt Dress (1492). These figures cover sales from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, and exclude any voided orders. Please note that products were grouped simply by their titles.
results.assumptions: Data range covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (treating 2026-09-30 as today). Voided orders are excluded. Products are grouped by title as requested.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by revenue?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, round(sum(l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN variants v USING (product_id) JOIN order_lines l USING (variant_id) JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;
results.answer: Your top-selling product by revenue over the past year was the One-Piece Swimsuit at $321,895.78, followed by the Shirt Dress at $224,593.45, High-Rise Jeans at $184,912.94, Wool Coat at $177,259.45, and the Straw Hat at $171,331.88. These figures represent total gross revenue including GST and discounts, excluding any voided orders between October 2025 and September 2026.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross revenue (line total after discounts, GST-inclusive) per product across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding voided orders.

results.question: What was our revenue in each month?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(orders.total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;
results.answer: Your monthly revenue ranged from $186,309.58 in February 2026 to $367,315.71 in June 2026, with December also being a strong month at $350,341.05. These figures include all non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026, calculated in Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Revenue is the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders, grouped by calendar month in Australia/Sydney time. Data covers 2025-10 to 2026-09.

results.question: Which month had the highest revenue, and how much was it?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(orders.total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY month ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Your highest revenue month was June 2026, bringing in $367,315.71 in gross sales. This covers all non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026 based on Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Which month had the highest revenue, and how much was it? Revenue is gross revenue (orders.total) for non-voided orders, grouped by calendar month in Australia/Sydney time across the entire data range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: How much revenue came from each sales channel?
results.sql: SELECT sales_channel, round(sum(total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY sales_channel ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Online sales brought in $2,070,833.88 AUD, while your in-store point of sale (pos) generated $1,251,096.83 AUD. These revenue figures are based on the total of all non-voided orders recorded for each channel.
results.assumptions: Revenue is calculated as the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders, grouped by sales_channel (online vs pos).

results.question: What is the revenue for each store location?
results.sql: SELECT l.name AS location_name, l.type AS location_type, ROUND(SUM(o.total)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue FROM orders o JOIN locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY l.location_id, l.name, l.type ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Your total gross revenue across all store locations for the entire period is led by the Online Store at $2,070,833.88 AUD, followed by the Surry Hills Boutique at $755,981.28 AUD and the Newtown Boutique at $495,115.55 AUD. These figures represent gross sales and exclude any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Revenue is gross revenue (sum of orders.total, excluding voided orders) grouped by each store location across the entire data period.

results.question: Compare the average order value for online and in-store orders.
results.sql: SELECT sales_channel, ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS average_order_value, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY sales_channel ORDER BY sales_channel;
results.answer: Online orders had a slightly higher average value than in-store orders, coming in at $194.13 compared to $187.49. These figures are based on 10,667 online orders and 6,673 in-store orders across the entire data period, with voided orders excluded.
results.assumptions: Comparing average order value (AOV) for online versus in-store (pos) channels across the entire data period, excluding voided orders.

results.question: Which product type sells the most units?
results.sql: SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, sum(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Accessories sell the most units, with a total of 8,771 units sold. This covers all non-voided orders across the entire data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. Product types were grouped using lowercased names to combine matching categories.
results.assumptions: Analysed all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Grouped by lowercased product types and summed quantities sold.

results.question: Which day of the week do we get the most orders, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'Day') AS day_of_week, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'Day'), extract(dow from orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Your shop gets the most orders on Saturdays, with a total of 3,468 orders. This is based on all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, converted to Sydney time. Please note that monetary values were not part of this specific count, as the result only tracked order volume.
results.assumptions: Analysed all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), converted timestamps to Australia/Sydney time, and grouped by day of the week.

results.question: At the peak hour of the day (Sydney time), how many online orders do we get in total?
results.sql: WITH hourly_orders AS (SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) AS order_hour, count(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE orders.sales_channel = 'online' AND orders.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1), peak_hour AS (SELECT order_hour FROM hourly_orders ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT hourly_orders.order_hour AS hour_of_day, hourly_orders.order_count AS total_online_orders FROM hourly_orders JOIN peak_hour USING (order_hour)
results.answer: Your peak hour for online orders is 8:00 PM (Sydney time), during which you received a total of 1,232 orders. This total includes all non-voided online orders across the entire data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (treated as today). Peak hour is determined by aggregating all non-voided online orders by their hour of the day in Australia/Sydney time across the entire data period.

results.question: How much have we given away in discounts in total?

results.answer: You have given away a total of $175,099.89 in discounts across all non-voided orders. This figure assumes all recorded discounts on active orders are accurate and fully accounted for.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: How much have we given away in discounts in total across all non-voided orders?

results.question: How many orders used the most popular discount code?

results.question: How many orders used the WELCOME10 code?

results.question: What is the total refunded amount for each refund reason?
results.sql: SELECT coalesce(reason, 'Unspecified') AS refund_reason, round(sum(amount), 2) AS total_refunded, count(*) AS refund_count FROM refunds GROUP BY reason ORDER BY total_refunded DESC;

These totals cover the entire dataset without any apparent missing data or truncation noted.
results.assumptions: Grouping refunds by their recorded reason. Unspecified covers null reasons. Total refunded is the sum of refunds.amount for each reason across the entire dataset.

results.question: What is the most common reason for refunds, and how many refunds is that?
results.sql: SELECT reason, count(*) AS refund_count, sum(amount) AS total_refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY reason ORDER BY refund_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: The most common reason for refunds is "Wrong size," with a total of 397 refunds amounting to $48,751.06 AUD. This total covers the entire data period provided.

results.answer: You had 468 non-voided orders placed during the Black Friday sale from November 27 to December 1, 2025. This count is based on orders recorded in Sydney local time.

results.question: How many customer accounts were created in 2026?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_accounts_created FROM customers WHERE (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date >= '2026-01-01' AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date <= '2026-09-30';
results.answer: You had 1,109 customer accounts created between January 1 and September 30, 2026. This count covers the available data range up to the end of September, so it does not include the final quarter of the year.

results.question: How many units did we sell in each size?
results.sql: SELECT v.size, SUM(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN variants v USING (variant_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.size IS NOT NULL GROUP BY v.size ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC;
results.answer: You sold a total of 32,871 units across all sizes, led by One Size with 8,771 units and Medium with 7,255 units. The remaining sizes include Small at 6,745, Large at 5,327, Extra Large at 2,412, and Extra Small at 2,361 units sold. This counts all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, and excludes any items where the size was not recorded.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: How many total units did we sell in each size across all non-voided orders for the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30)? Sizes with NULL values are excluded.

results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND lower(p.product_type) = 'dress'
results.answer: Your dresses brought in a total of $542,989.65 in gross revenue. This covers all unvoided dress orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026. Keep in mind this figure is GST-inclusive and already factors in any line-level discounts applied.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as gross revenue from all orders where financial_status <> 'voided' for products of type 'dress', covering the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is GST-inclusive and includes line-level discounts.

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity) * 100.0 / sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 2) AS gross_profit_margin_percentage FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin across all valid orders is 58.32%. This calculation is based on revenue excluding GST and excludes any order lines that were missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What is our overall gross profit margin across all non-voided orders? Revenue is taken ex-GST (divided by 1.1), and order lines with missing cost data (NULL) are excluded as per business rules.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, round(sum(((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * l.quantity))::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5
results.answer: Your top-selling product by gross profit is the One-Piece Swimsuit at $165,884.48 AUD, followed by the Shirt Dress at $130,441.22 AUD, Straw Hat at $108,854.01 AUD, High-Rise Jeans at $104,531.12 AUD, and Wool Coat at $89,912.11 AUD. These figures exclude any items missing cost data, which could affect the final rankings.
results.assumptions: Gross profit is calculated as net ex-GST revenue minus total unit cost (variants.cost * quantity). Variants with NULL cost are excluded from the margin calculation.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql: SELECT round(sum(o.total) - coalesce((SELECT sum(r.amount) FROM refunds r), 0), 2) AS net_revenue FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Your total net revenue after refunds across the entire dataset from October 2025 to September 2026 is $3,205,298.79 AUD. This figure calculates non-voided orders minus all refunds. Please note that this total assumes all orders in the dataset were successfully processed and does not account for potential future adjustments or chargebacks.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What is our total net revenue after refunds across the entire dataset (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026)? Revenue includes non-voided orders minus all refunds.

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 0) AS NUMERIC), 2) AS percentage_with_refund FROM orders o LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided';
results.answer: Out of all your non-voided orders, 5.7% had a refund between October 2025 and September 2026. This percentage is based on orders having at least one associated refund during that time.
results.assumptions: Calculated the percentage of non-voided orders that have at least one associated refund across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(rl.quantity) AS units_refunded FROM refund_lines rl JOIN refunds r ON rl.refund_id = r.refund_id JOIN order_lines ol ON rl.order_line_id = ol.order_line_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_refunded DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: The product with the most units refunded across the entire data period is the One-Piece Swimsuit, with 165 units returned. This total excludes any voided orders based on our standard filtering rules.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Which product has had the most units refunded, and how many across the entire data period, excluding voided orders.

results.question: How many different customers have placed an order?
results.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers_with_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: A total of 2,909 different customers have placed an order. This count is based on unique customer IDs from non-voided orders and excludes any guest checkouts where the customer ID was missing.
results.assumptions: Counting unique customer IDs from non-voided orders, excluding guest checkouts where customer_id is NULL.

results.question: What percentage of orders were placed by guests with no customer account?
results.sql: SELECT round(100.0 * sum(case when customer_id is null then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 2) AS guest_order_percentage FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: Guests without an account placed 22.47% of your orders over the entire data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. This percentage is based on non-voided orders only.
results.assumptions: Calculated as the percentage of non-voided orders where customer_id is NULL over all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(orders.total), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' AND orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AND orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
results.answer: Your total revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 in July, $282,129.97 in August, and $278,068.87 in September 2026. These figures represent the gross sales from all non-voided orders for each month.
results.assumptions: Treating today as 2026-09-30. The last 3 months are July, August, and September 2026. Revenue is gross orders.total for non-voided orders.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale (19 Jun - 5 Jul)' AS period,
    sum(total) AS revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-06 00:00:00'
),
pre_eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (2 Jun - 18 Jun)' AS period,
    sum(total) AS revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-02 00:00:00'
    AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
)
SELECT * FROM eofy_period
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM pre_eofy_period;
results.answer: During the EOFY sale, your revenue jumped to $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders, which is a strong increase compared to the $186,171.83 from 794 orders in the 17 days right before the sale. This comparison assumes gross revenue with voided orders excluded over two equal 17-day periods.
results.assumptions: Compared the EOFY sale period (19 June to 5 July 2026, inclusive, 17 days) with the immediately preceding 17-day period (2 June to 18 June 2026). Revenue is gross revenue (orders.total) excluding voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines ol ON v.variant_id = ol.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC LIMIT 3;
results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units over the full data period are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These figures include sales summed across all variants and exclude any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Date range: full data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Excluded voided orders. Units sold are summed across all variants for each product title.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id HAVING count(order_id) >= 3) t
results.answer: You have 1,640 unique registered customers who have placed three or more non-voided orders. This count includes all valid orders across your entire dataset, though it excludes any orders where the customer ID was left blank.
results.assumptions: Counting unique registered customers (customer_id not null) who have placed 3 or more non-voided orders across the entire dataset.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation includes all recorded refund events across the available data.
results.assumptions: Calculated the difference in days between the order creation timestamp and the refund creation timestamp for all refund events.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?

results.answer: Your shop made $944,363.46 in revenue from orders that used a discount. This total covers all non-voided orders across the entire available date range from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN variants v USING (variant_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Camel sold the most units during the winter of 2026 with a total of 1,050 units sold. This count excludes any voided orders, per standard sales rules.
results.assumptions: Winter 2026 is defined as June 1, 2026 to August 31, 2026 in Australia/Sydney time. Revenue and unit counts exclude voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, ROUND(SUM(o.total)::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more total revenue than weekends, with weekdays generating 2,147,980.22 AUD across 11,153 orders compared to 1,173,950.49 AUD from 6,187 weekend orders. This comparison assumes standard five-day weekdays and two-day weekends evaluated in Australia/Sydney time from October 2025 through September 2026.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of orders.total for non-voided orders. Weekdays are Monday to Friday (ISODOW 1-5), and weekends are Saturday and Sunday (ISODOW 6-7), evaluated in Australia/Sydney time across the entire data range (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql:
WITH product_sales AS ( 
  SELECT 
    lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, 
    p.title AS product_title, 
    sum(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold, 
    row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(l.quantity) DESC) as rn 
  FROM order_lines l 
  JOIN orders o USING (order_id) 
  JOIN variants v USING (variant_id) 
  JOIN products p USING (product_id) 
  WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' 
  GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title 
) 
SELECT 
  product_type, 
  product_title AS best_selling_product, 
  total_units_sold 
FROM product_sales 
WHERE rn = 1 
ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC;
results.answer: Your best-selling products by category, led by the One-Piece Swimsuit in swimwear at 4,043 units and the Straw Hat in accessories at 3,619 units, are ranked by total units sold in non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026. The remaining top sellers include the Linen Wrap Skirt (1,804), Shirt Dress (1,492), Ribbed Tank (1,395), High-Rise Jeans (1,295), Wool Coat (828), and Merino Crew Jumper (526). These figures cover all valid sales data for the entire twelve-month period with product types normalized to lowercase.
results.assumptions: Ranked products by total units sold per product type across all non-voided orders for the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Product types are normalized to lowercase.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING sum(l.quantity) > 1) t
results.answer: There were 8,908 orders that contained more than one unit in total. This count excludes any voided orders and looks at the combined quantity across all lines in each order.
results.assumptions: Excluding voided orders. Counting orders where the sum of quantities across all order lines is greater than 1.
